en: I'm Wayne. I'm 14.
Do you live near here? Nice to meet you, mister.
Oh, it's you, mister.
Are you still all on your own?
Yep. It's just me, Wayne.
Papa and Mama are busy,
so I'm always minding the house.
You came again, mister?
Oh! You're back again, mister?
What kind of work do you do, mister?
<That's a secret>
<I'm looking for someone>
note: Answer choice (no used_in), as #690; leads to msg 21699 (#732).

en: Really? Is it someone you like, mister?
Keep at it, OK?
Hey, take me outside sometime, mister.
Hello, mister.
Wow, come in, mister!
I'm glad when you come over, mister.
Even a young boy like this
note: Player's thought; three #265 dots follow: 'Even a young boy like this...'

en: Oh, it's

note: 'Mister' moved into the #739 variant for msg 21900: 'Huh? Mister {NAME}!?'

en: What's the matter?
Oh, no real reason.
I just felt like seeing you.
...I know how it is. Being all alone
gets lonely, doesn't it?
Come over here, mister.
I'm sorry...
Aaaaaaah!!
I just need you to help me for a little while.
, you are my one true master.
Your orders
note: #152 '...' follows: 'Your orders...'. Shared by many servants.

en: Good heavens, my joints ache.
And I feel as if I haven't slept enough
, my master
note: After the name; #152 '...' follows: '{NAME}, my master...' (as #0). Every use is servant mode; next row starts a sentence.

en: Come, give me any order you wish
I always feel sluggish and I can't shake this fatigue.
And there are cuts all over me... Why?
Hm? And who might you be?
I can't have people just walking in like this.
Did someone give you an introduction?
Ah, forgive me.
I thought I really should come and greet you.
You have business with me, Gilbert?
I serve as Mayor of London.
Please take views on city policy to city hall.
Mayor Gilbert, it's me,
note: Name follows on the next line: 'Mayor Gilbert, it's me, / {NAME}. Have you forgotten?'

en: . Have you forgotten?
My apologies for the other day.
Hm? ...Ah, you're the fellow from before.
And what business might you have with me?
I've no time for idle callers. Good day.
I'd rather you didn't wander in here for no reason.
I strive every day to improve the city's affairs.
Naturally, I respect the citizens' opinions too.
If you're not an idle caller, you're welcome.
Oh, hello,
I hear you've been making inquiries around
the city. Is it for your work?
<Yes, it is>
<I have my reasons>
Oh... I see.
I don't know what your work may be, but do
take care not to make the citizens uneasy.
I see. Are you looking for someone?
note: No used_in: the decoder shows #3331 at the start of msgs 25485/26032 (a branch-op misread, as noted in the slice-000 report); #785 is the first line there, then #786/#787.

en: London has its detectives too, so why not
try hiring one?
Good grief, you again?
Well, I'm used to your sudden visits by now.
For once, perhaps I'll talk about myself.
You must think me an unsociable man.
My work is the only way I can express myself.
Perhaps I can't claim my politics are all
clean. But this city needs me.
I believe that, and so I work on as mayor.
You again?
I can't fathom why you're so eager to come
here. Do you have an interest in politics?
Yes? Who is it?
